history: The Dodge Neon SRT-4 emerged from Chrysler's Street and Racing Technology (SRT) division in 2003 as a factory-built performance compact aimed squarely at the growing sport compact tuner market. Built on the second-generation Neon platform, the SRT-4 transformed an economy car into a genuine performance machine capable of embarrassing far more expensive vehicles.

Development was led by the SRT team under engineer Dan Knott, who pushed for a high-boost turbocharged setup rather than a naturally aspirated approach. The result was a 2.4-liter turbocharged four-cylinder producing 230 horsepower and 250 lb-ft of torque — numbers that shocked the industry for a sub-$20,000 car.

The SRT-4 quickly earned a cult following among enthusiasts, particularly for its immense tuning potential. With basic bolt-on modifications, owners could push output well past 300 horsepower while retaining daily drivability. The car competed directly with the Honda Civic Si, Volkswagen GTI, and Subaru WRX — and frequently beat all of them on a dollar-per-horsepower basis.

Production ran from the 2003 to 2005 model years, with approximately 16,000 units produced total. The car was discontinued when the Neon platform was retired, though a spiritual successor was considered for the Caliber platform before being cancelled.
did_you_know: The SRT-4 was one of the first factory cars to offer a dealer-installed Stage 1 and Stage 2 upgrade kit — essentially factory-backed performance tuning. Stage 2 pushed output to 260 hp with a larger turbocharger and supporting mods, all covered under warranty.

trims.name: SRT-4 Base
trims.description: The standard SRT-4 with the full performance package. Included 17" wheels, Brembo front brakes, strut tower brace, and the 230hp turbo engine.

trims.name: ACR Package
trims.description: American Club Racer add-on. Koni adjustable shocks, front strut bar, rear sway bar, short-throw shifter, and deleted A/C + radio for weight savings.

trims.name: Stage 1 Kit
trims.description: Factory upgrade: larger intercooler, boost controller, and ECU tune. Bumped output to approximately 250 hp. Warranty-legal when dealer-installed.

trims.name: Stage 2 Kit
trims.description: Larger turbocharger, upgraded injectors, full retune. Produced approximately 260 hp from the factory. Rare and highly collectible today.

variants.name: SRT-4 ACR
variants.description: The performance-focused ACR (American Club Racer) package stripped out creature comforts in exchange for Koni suspension and chassis bracing — making it the weapon of choice for autocross and track day events.

variants.name: Stage 2 Factory Car
variants.description: Extremely rare dealer-installed Stage 2 cars are considered the holy grail of SRT-4 collecting. With documented dealer installation and original paperwork, these are among the most sought-after examples.

variants.name: Mopar Stage Kits
variants.description: While not a separate model, the factory Mopar Stage 1 and Stage 2 performance kits were unique in the industry — factory-backed power upgrades that maintained emissions compliance and warranty coverage.
